h1: Halation effect: what it is and how to get the film glow on iPhone
card_summary: The red glow around lights of tungsten cinema film, on your night photos.
quick_answer: Halation is the red-orange glow around bright lights on film without an anti-halation layer, made famous by tungsten-balanced cinema film used for stills. iPhone photos never show it. In Halatto, open a night photo with lights in the frame and pick Tungsten 800: red halos around lights, teal shadows and film grain. Lower the strength for skin, raise grain for a grittier frame.
intro: Neon signs, street lamps, car lights and candles all bloom on certain night films. That glow is what makes night photos feel like a movie still instead of a phone snapshot.
Here is what causes it, which photos it works on and how to get it on iPhone.

sections.heading: What is halation?
paragraphs: Halation is the red or orange glow that spreads around bright lights in a photo shot on film. Light passes through the film, bounces off the back of the film base and exposes the red-sensitive layer a second time, so street lamps, neon and headlights get a soft red halo.
Digital sensors do not do this, which is why the same night scene from an iPhone looks clean and hard. A halation effect puts that glow back.

sections.heading: What causes halation
paragraphs: Bright light passes through the film, reflects off the back of the base and exposes the red-sensitive layer again around the highlight. Most still films have a layer that stops this; cinema film with that layer removed does not, so every light gets a red halo.
Tungsten-balanced film also renders artificial light neutral and pushes shadows and daylight toward teal, which gives the classic night palette.

sections.heading: Photos that suit halation
list: City streets with signs, lamps and traffic lights.
Bars, concerts, kitchens with warm bulbs in frame.
Portraits in front of lights, with highlights in the background.
Not daylight landscapes: without bright points of light there is nothing to glow.

steps.heading: Step by step: night film in Halatto

items.name: Open a night photo
items.text: Pick a photo with lights in the frame.

items.name: Choose Tungsten 800
items.text: Tap Tungsten 800 in the Looks strip and compare with the divider.

items.name: Balance it
items.text: Lower the strength if skin turns too teal; raise grain for a grittier look.

items.name: Save or shoot live
items.text: Save the photo, or open the built-in camera with Tungsten 800 to shoot the rest of the night.

tips.heading: Tips
items: Slightly underexposed night photos keep the glow from washing out.
Avoid night mode's long, bright exposures; a regular quick shot looks more like film.
Pair with a soft red light leak for a music-video feel.

faq.question: Is Tungsten 800 a CineStill 800T filter?
faq.answer: It is Halatto's own night cinema film look in that style: red halos around lights and teal shadows. Halatto is not affiliated with CineStill.

faq.question: Can I add halation to a daylight photo?
faq.answer: It needs bright points of light to glow around, so daylight photos show little effect.

faq.question: Does the iPhone have a halation setting?
faq.answer: No. The Camera and Photos apps have no halation or glow control.
